memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If the neighbor is poor, do not go to sleep with their pledge in your possession. Return their cloak by sunset so that your neighbor may sleep in it. Then they will thank you, and it will be regarded as a righteous act in the sight of the Lord your God. - Deut 24:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
For a poor person, a cloak was often their only covering, their blanket against the cold night. So if someone gave their cloak as a pledge for a loan, God commanded that it be returned by sunset, so they would have something to keep warm through the night. The lender's security mattered less than the poor person's basic comfort and survival. God says returning the cloak would be counted as "a righteous act" in His sight.

What a beautiful window into God's heart. He notices whether a poor person will be cold at night. He cares about their comfort more than about a lender's convenience. And He counts such compassion as righteousness, something precious and pleasing to Him. In God's economy, mercy toward the needy is treasured.

This teaches us that true righteousness is not merely about religious rituals but includes practical compassion for those in need. God delights when His people care for the poor and vulnerable in tangible ways. The New Testament echoes this, teaching that pure and genuine faith shows itself in caring for those in distress (Jas 1:27). When we meet real needs, returning the "cloak" to someone who is cold, we reflect the heart of God and please Him. Christ Himself is the supreme example, laying down everything for our sake. Who around you is "cold" and in need, and how might God be inviting you to show them practical compassion?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you see practical compassion as part of righteousness?
2. Who around you is "cold" and in need right now?
3. How can you meet a real need this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You treasure compassion toward the needy. Open my eyes to real needs around me and help me meet them with love. Amen.
